entry.title: Statistics for ML #99 — Causal Inference: DAGs, Do-Calculus

link.title: Statistics for ML #99 — Causal Inference: DAGs, Do-Calculus

entry.content:
Causal Inference: DAGs, Do-Calculus

Post #99/100 in the Statistics for ML series — Md Salek Miah Statistician & ML Researcher SUST, Bangladesh.

Causal Inference moves beyond correlation to answer: “Does X cause Y?” This is the central question in public health policy.

DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs)

A DAG encodes causal assumptions. Arrows represent direct causal effects. Used to identify confounders, mediators, and colliders.

Tools: Dagitty (web-based), dagitty R package — used in our DHS research for confounder selection.

Do-Calculus (Pearl’s Framework)

\(P(Y | do(X=x)) \neq P(Y | X=x)\)

The do-operator represents intervening to set X, vs observing X.

Key Concepts

Concept Description Example
Confounder Causes both X and Y Wealth → ANC visits AND delivery location
Mediator On causal path X→M→Y ANC → knowledge → SBA
Collider Caused by both X and Y Conditioning on collider opens non-causal path 
library(dagitty)
library(ggdag)

# DAG for SBA research
dag <- dagitty('dag {
  Wealth -> ANC_visits
  Wealth -> SBA
  ANC_visits -> SBA
  Education -> Wealth
  Education -> SBA
  Rural -> ANC_visits
  Rural -> SBA
}')

# Find minimal adjustment set for ANC -> SBA
adjustmentSets(dag, exposure="ANC_visits", outcome="SBA")
ggdag(dag, layout="circle") + theme_dag()

entry.title: Statistics for ML #57 — Multicollinearity & VIF
entry.content:
Multicollinearity & VIF

Post #57 of 100 in the Statistics for ML series by Md Salek Miah — Statistician, SUST Bangladesh.

What You Will Learn

The Multicollinearity & VIF is one of the core building blocks of quantitative research. This post covers:

  1. Mathematical definition — precise and complete
  2. Intuitive explanation — what it means in plain language
  3. Public health application — real examples from DHS survey research
  4. Python implementation — ready-to-run code
  5. R implementation — for epidemiologists and survey analysts
  6. ML connection — how this concept appears in modern algorithms

Core Mathematics

The Multicollinearity & VIF formalises how we model relationships between variables and make predictions.

Python Code

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# Multicollinearity & VIF — implementation example
# Full code available at: github.com/muhammadsalek
print("Post #57: Multicollinearity & VIF")

# Example: Load DHS-style data
np.random.seed(42)
n = 1000
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'anc_visits': np.random.poisson(3.2, n),
    'birth_weight': np.random.normal(3100, 480, n),
    'sba': np.random.binomial(1, 0.67, n),
    'wealth_q': np.random.randint(1, 6, n),
    'rural': np.random.binomial(1, 0.65, n)
})

# Apply Multicollinearity & VIF concepts here
print(data.describe())

library(survey)
library(broom)

  • Model specification for binary health outcomes (SBA, stunting, IPV)
